recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless FHIR-I reopens SubscriptionTopic trigger/filter semantics; adding another restatement would be redundant with the maintained trigger, queryCriteria, and Subscription.filterBy definitions.
issue_request: FHIR-39025 asked whether SubscriptionTopic.resourceTrigger.queryCriteria.resultForCreate, resultForDelete, and requireBoth are server/topic-definition controls or client-overridable Subscription request values, and requested clearer narrative; FHIR-I resolved it as Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5, requiring more documentation and declining to rename the elements.
initial_application: Commit ba83bbc88184d7b8c6140c49f65b0e693eb35ea8 applied FHIR-39025 by clarifying the SubscriptionTopic StructureDefinition definitions/comments for supportedInteraction, resultForCreate, resultForDelete, and requireBoth, and by adding SubscriptionTopic narrative for queryCriteria behavior during create/delete/update interactions plus trigger/filter separation.
additional_context: The R5 resourceTrigger path has since been refactored to current SubscriptionTopic.trigger naming, with fhir.ini aliases preserving the old names. Current source keeps SubscriptionTopic active in the build, separates trigger criteria from client filters, defines the queryCriteria flags on SubscriptionTopic.trigger, and leaves Subscription with filterBy fields only. FHIR-39028 and FHIR-50619 are same-family/later SubscriptionTopic clarifications already represented on the combined branch and they refine rather than reverse the FHIR-39025 rule.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative source already says triggers are topic-level tests used to generate notifications for any Subscription linked to the topic, explains resultForCreate/resultForDelete/requireBoth behavior in the queryCriteria section and table, and distinguishes those controls from Subscription.filterBy client values.
